observations.topic: Husher/binder failure is not absence of raising
observations.data: In 100 held-out runs, mixed husher/binder averaged 3.82 raised boneservants; pure binders averaged 5.83, yet achieved 5%/0% wins vs 12% pure husher.
observations.interpretation: Raising has real opportunity cost. It occurs before ordinary attacks and consumes shared cooldown. Root binding occurs only on a normal attack, so raising and control compete for actions.
observations.nextTest: Binder 15–30% with thornling damage dealers; labelled shared-corpse context with broodcap.

observations.topic: Brood/spore pair partly substitutes the same function
observations.data: Held-out mixed brood/spore averaged 8.06 brood spawns; pure brood averaged 22.49. Wins were 5% mixed versus 7% pure spore and 2% pure brood.
observations.interpretation: Broodcap already creates sporelings. Its children are rank 1/strength 1 even when the parent is rank 3; initial rank 3 sporelings front-load stronger bodies. This is timing and sustain substitution, not an automatic superadditive pair.
observations.nextTest: Broodcap+mender at low support fraction; consecutive-wave persistence with equal timing and explicit corpse resources.

observations.topic: Guardian pair comparator is saturated and chunky
observations.data: Held-out guardian/bulwark won 82% versus 96% pure guardian. In small discovery guardian+mender often tied 100% pure guardian.
observations.interpretation: At the frozen threat weight, pure guardians often saturate victory. A guardian costs 5.76 threat at rank 3, so rounding can add a large body to the pure comparator. Larger scales and lower threat bands are needed for a meaningful boundary.
observations.nextTest: Guardian+mender at scales 3/4, threat ratios.4/.7, medic share 15–30%.

observations.topic: Field guardians are not the full boss-gate encounter
observations.interpretation: Natural guardians are difficulty-specific boss garrisons with leash, regeneration and party-readiness behaviour. Arena rank 3 guardian uses the actual generic monster archetype, without those gate controls. Hypothetical allied-pair superiority is not a required property of the natural boss encounter.

observations.topic: Support stalemate is different from defeat
observations.data: Pure menders timed out 100/100 in the first held-out field context and 99/100 in two later field contexts.
observations.interpretation: Low monster victory alone does not mean a weak support. Menders can deny clearing while failing to finish heroes. Report hero wins, monster wins, timeouts and effective healing independently.

observations.topic: Equal initial threat is an experimental assumption
observations.interpretation: Heroes have observable recruitment costs; monsters do not have a purchase price. THREAT values are fixed estimates, not game prices. Actual lairs produce basic/support recipes with level-dependent counts. It is inappropriate to recalibrate those weights after seeing outcomes just to force every pair to beat both homogeneous controls.
observations.nextTest: Keep frozen weights; test role-appropriate support fractions and resource/timing conditions, then validate selected contexts on fresh seeds.
